description: FOMO60K is a subset of FOMO300K containing 60,529 brain MRI scans from 13,900 MRI sessions across 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available datasets. Unlike FOMO300K, all scans in FOMO60K were affinely co-registered within each session to the highest-resolution image, and either skull-stripped or defaced. It was developed in parallel with the FOMO25 challenge at MICCAI 2025 to support self-supervised learning for medical imaging.
name: FOMO60K
publisher: University of Copenhagen / Pioneer Centre For AI
rai:dataBiases: Existing large-scale datasets are often curated for specific diseases or patient populations and typically follow homogeneous imaging protocols with limited pathological variability. FOMO60K was designed to include both clinical- and research-grade images and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability to be more representative of real-world population-level data. The dataset includes scans with large brain anomalies to address the lack of pathological diversity in prior datasets.
rai:dataCollection: FOMO60K was aggregated from 16 publicly available datasets. All data were obtained from publicly available sources, each governed by specific licenses or data use agreements. Each constituent dataset was collected under protocols approved by the respective institutional review boards of the original studies. No new human subjects research was conducted for this data aggregation project.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Brain MRI scans from 16 publicly available source datasets, including MGH Wild, OpenNeuro subsets (SOOP, NIMH, DLBS, IDEAS, ARC, MBSR, UCLA, QTAB, AOMIC ID1000), BraTS-GEN, OASIS1, OASIS2, MSD Braintumor, IXI, and NKI. Sequences include T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR, T1ce, DWI, T2*, PD, SWI, GRE, and minIP. Images were provided in various formats and some were already skull-stripped or defaced by the dataset providers.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All scans in FOMO60K were affinely co-registered within each session to the highest-resolution image. Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) when images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features. For DWI, b0 volumes were extracted separately and b1000 shell volumes were averaged into a single 3D image.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MRI preprocessing for FOMO60K comprised three main steps: (1) reorienting images to RAS orientation, (2) affine co-registration using mri_coreg from FreeSurfer 7.4.1 with default parameters (scans aligned to the highest spatial resolution image within each session), and (3) skull-stripping using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) when images were not already defaced or skull-stripped. For DWI scans in 4D format, if a b0 volume was available it was extracted and saved separately; for the b1000 shell, volumes were averaged into a single representative 3D image. No trace ADC computation or additional b-value shell grouping was performed.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available. Users must accept a data use agreement before downloading FOMO60K.
rai:dataSocialImpact: FOMO60K was developed to lower barriers to entry for self-supervised learning in neuroimaging by providing a publicly available, preprocessed collection. It was developed in parallel with the FOMO25 challenge at MICCAI 2025 to catalyze progress in self-supervised learning for medical imaging.
rai:dataUseCases: FOMO60K is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging. It was developed in parallel with the FOMO25 challenge at MICCAI 2025 to catalyze progress in self-supervised learning for medical imaging.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) — used for skull-stripping by generating segmentation masks of brain structures; mri_coreg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) — used for affine co-registration of scans within each session.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains brain MRI scans from human subjects, along with demographic information including age, sex, handedness, and diagnostic group. All scans were either skull-stripped or defaced to protect subject identity. Each constituent dataset was collected under protocols approved by the respective institutional review boards.

evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MRI preprocessing for FOMO60K comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS orientation (as in FOMO300K), affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. All scans were first reoriented to RAS and affinely co-registered using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.1938, with default parameters. Within each MRI session, scans were aligned to the image with the highest spatial resolution to preserve most anatomical detail.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Unlike FOMO300K, all scans in FOMO60K were affinely co-registered within each session to the highest-resolution image, and either skull-stripped or defaced (see more details below). Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg939(FreeSurfer 7.4.1), which outputs segmentation masks of brain structures. These masks were used to define the brain extraction region. Skull-stripping was only applied when the images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features that could compromise anonymization.
